https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: active safety system
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Active safety systems are vehicle systems that sense and monitor conditions inside and outside the vehicle for the purpose of identifying perceived present and potential dangers to the vehicle, occupants, and/or other road users, and automatically intervene to help avoid or mitigate potential collisions via various methods, including alerts to the driver, vehicle system adjustments, and/or active control of the vehicle subsystems (brakes, throttle, suspension, etc.).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: automated driving system
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The hardware and software that are collectively capable of performing the entire DDT on a sustained basis, regardless of whether it is limited to a specific operational design domain (ODD); this term is used specifically to describe a Level 3, 4, or 5 driving automation system.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: ADS dedicated vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: ADS-equipped vehicle designed for driverless operation under routine/normal operating conditions during all trips within its given ODD (if any)

annotations.example: A Level 4 ADS-DV designed to operate exclusively within a corporate campus where it picks up and discharges passengers along a specific route specified by the ADS-DV dispatcher.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: ADS dual-mode vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: ADS-equipped vehicle designed to enable either driverless operation under routine/normal operating conditions within its given ODD (if any), or operation by an in-vehicle driver, for complete trips

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: ADS equipped vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: vehicle equipped with an automated driving system

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: campus
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: collection of buildings and grounds that belong to a given institution, either academic or non-academic

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: central business district
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: commercial and business center of a city

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: city centre
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: commercial, cultural and often geographic heart of a city

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: conditional driving automation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The sustained and ODD-specific performance by an ADS of the entire DDT under routine/normal operation (see 3.27) with the expectation that the DDT fallback-ready user is receptive to ADS-issued requests to intervene, as well as to DDT performance-relevant system failures in other vehicle systems, and will respond appropriately.

annotations.example: An ADS feature capable of performing the entire DDT in low-speed, stop-and-go freeway traffic.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: confined geographic location
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: region (point, line, or area) on Earth's surface or elsewhere

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: congested traffic
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: traffic that is characterized by slower speeds, longer trip times, and increased vehicular queueing

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: conventional vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: vehicle designed to be operated by an in-vehicle driver during part or all of every trip

annotations.example: A vehicle equipped with Level 1 adaptive cruise control, Level 1 lane centering, and a Level 3 ADS feature designed to perform the complete DDT during traffic jams on fully access-controlled freeways. The Level 3 ADS traffic jam feature requires the user to operate the vehicle on the way to the freeway before engaging the feature, as well as again operating the vehicle upon exiting the freeway in order to complete the trip.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: corporate campus
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: collection of buildings and grounds that belong to a given corporation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: corporate campus, specific route
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: specific route in a corporate campus

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: DDT performance-relevant system failure
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A malfunction in a driving automation system and/or other vehicle system that prevents the driving automation system from reliably performing its portion of the DDT on a sustained basis, including the complete DDT, that it would otherwise perform.

annotations.example: A Level 1 driver support feature that performs the lateral vehicle motion control subtask of the DDT experiences a DDT performance-relevant system failure in one of its cameras, which prevents it from reliably detecting lane markings. The feature causes a malfunction indication message to be displayed in the center console at the same time that the feature automatically disengages, requiring the driver to immediately resume performing the lateral vehicle motion control subtask of the DDT.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: daylight
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: period when there is natural light from the sun

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: designated freeway, high-volume traffic
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: high-volume traffic on a designated freeway

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: dispatch in driveless operation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: To place an ADS-equipped vehicle into service in driverless operation by engaging the ADS

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: driver assistance
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The sustained and ODD-specific execution by a driving automation system of either the lateral or the longitudinal vehicle motion control subtask of the DDT (but not both simultaneously) with the expectation that the driver performs the remainder of the DDT.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: driver support DAS feature
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A general term for Level 1 and Level 2 driving automation system features.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: driverless operation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: on-road operation of an ADS-equipped vehicle that is unoccupied, or in which on-board users are not drivers or in-vehicle fallback-ready users

annotations.example: A Level 4 ADS-DV is dispatched in driverless operation for purposes of providing transportation service.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: driverless operation dispatcher
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: user(s) who dispatches an ADS-equipped vehicle(s) in driverless operation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: driverless operation dispatching entity
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An entity that dispatches an ADS-equipped vehicle(s) in driverless operation.

annotations.example: A fleet of Level 4 closed campus ADS-dedicated vehicles is placed into service by a driverless operation dispatching entity, which engages the ADS for each vehicle after verifying its operational readiness and disengages the ADS when each vehicle is taken out of service.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: driving automation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The performance by hardware/software systems of part or all of the DDT on a sustained basis.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: driving automation system
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The hardware and software that are collectively capable of performing part or all of the DDT on a sustained basis; this term is used generically to describe any system capable of Level 1 to 5 driving automation.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: DAS feature
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A Level 1-5 driving automation system’s design-specific functionality at a given level of driving automation within a particular ODD, if applicable.

annotations.example: A Level 3 ADS feature that performs the DDT, excluding DDT fallback, in high-volume traffic on fully access-controlled freeways.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: DDT fallback-ready user
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: user of a vehicle equipped with an engaged Level 3 ADS feature who is properly qualified and able to operate the vehicle and is receptive to ADS-issued requests to intervene and to evident DDT performance-relevant system failures in the vehicle compelling him or her to perform the DDT fallback

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: dynamic driving subtask
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A real-time operational or tactical function required to operate a vehicle in on-road traffic.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: dynamic driving task
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: All of the real-time operational and tactical functions required to operate a vehicle in on-road traffic, excluding the strategic functions such as trip scheduling and selection of destinations and waypoints, and including, without limitation, the following subtasks: Lateral vehicle motion control via steering (operational); Longitudinal vehicle motion control via acceleration and deceleration (operational); Monitoring the driving environment via object and event detection, recognition, classification, and response preparation (operational and tactical); Object and event response execution (operational and tactical); Maneuver planning (tactical); Enhancing conspicuity via lighting, sounding the horn, signaling, gesturing, etc. (tactical).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: DDT fallback
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The response by the user to either perform the DDT or achieve a minimal risk condition (1) after occurrence of a DDT performance-relevant system failure(s), or (2) upon operational design domain (ODD) exit, or the response by an ADS to achieve minimal risk condition, given the same circumstances.

annotations.example: A Level 1 adaptive cruise control (ACC) feature experiences a system failure that causes the feature to stop performing its intended function. The human driver performs the DDT fallback by resuming performance of the complete DDT.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: failure migration strategy
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: vehicle function (not an ADS function) designed to automatically bring an ADS-equipped vehicle to a controlled stop in path following either: (1) prolonged failure of the fallback-ready user of a Level 3 ADS feature to perform the fallback after the ADS has issued a request to intervene, or (2) occurrence of a system failure or external event so catastrophic that it incapacitates the ADS, which can no longer perform vehicle motion control in order to perform the fallback and achieve a minimal risk condition. (See 8.6.)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: fair weather
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: weather conditions conducive to driving such as good visibility and dry road surface

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: falling weather
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: weather characterized by heavy rain, snow or hail that makes driving difficult

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: feature
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Indicates a built-in feature, accessory, or component of the vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: fleet operation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The activities that support the management of a fleet of ADS-equipped vehicles in driverless operation, which may include, without limitation: Ensuring operational readiness; Dispatching ADS-equipped vehicles in driverless operation (i.e., engaging the ADSs prior to placing the vehicles in service on public roads); Authorizing each trip (e.g., payment, trip route selection); Providing fleet asset management services to vehicles while in-use (e.g., managing emergencies, summoning or providing remote assistance as needed, responding to customer requests and break-downs); Serving as the responsible agent vis-a-vis law enforcement, emergency responders and other authorities for vehicles while in use; Disengaging the ADS at the end of service; Performing vehicle repair and maintenance as needed.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: foggy weather
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: weather characterized by fog that reduces visibility on the road

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: freeway
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: wide road for fast-moving traffic, especially in the US, with a limited number of places at which drivers can enter and leave it

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: freeway, low speed, optimal road maintenance, fair weather
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: fully access-controlled freeway in low-speed traffic under fair weather conditions and optimal road maintenance

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: freeway, traffic jam
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: traffic jam on a freeway

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: full driving automation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The sustained and unconditional (i.e., not ODD-specific) performance by an ADS of the entire DDT and DDT fallback.

annotations.example: A vehicle with an ADS that, once programmed with a destination, is capable of operating the vehicle throughout complete trips on public roadways, regardless of the starting and end points or intervening road, traffic, and weather conditions.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: full-trip feature
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: ADS features that operate a vehicle throughout complete trips

annotations.example: A Level 4 ADS-DV is dispatched in driverless operation for purposes of providing ride-hailing services to customers located within its geo-fenced area of operation.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: geofenced area
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: geographic area with a virtual boundary, defined by GPS or RFID technology, that enables software to trigger a response when a mobile device enters or leaves a particular area

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: high driving automation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The sustained and ODD-specific performance by an ADS of the entire DDT and DDT fallback’.

annotations.example: A Level 4 ADS feature capable of performing the entire DDT during sustained operation on a motorway or freeway (i.e., within its ODD). (Note: The presence of a user in the driver’s seat who is capable of performing the DDT is envisioned in this example, as driver performance of the DDT would have been necessary before entering, and would again be necessary after leaving, the motorway or freeway. Thus, such a feature would alert the user that s/he should resume vehicle operation shortly before exiting the ODD, but if the user fails to respond to such an alert, the ADS will nevertheless perform the DDT fallback and achieve a minimal risk condition automatically.)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: high-volume traffic
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: traffic with a volume of more than 50,000 AADT (Annual Average Daily Traffic)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: highway
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: main road, especially one that connects towns or cities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: human driver
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: user who performs in real time part or all of the DDT and/or DDT fallback for a particular vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: human user
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: general term referencing the human role in driving automation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: in-vehicle driver
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: driver who manually exercises in-vehicle braking, accelerating, steering, and transmission gear selection input devices in order to operate a vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: in-vehicle DDT fallback-ready user
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: fallback-ready user of a conventional vehicle with an engaged Level 3 ADS feature who is seated in the driver’s seat

annotations.example: A Level 3 ADS sub-trip feature designed to perform the DDT in congested traffic on certain freeways encounters emergency responders who are rerouting traffic to the exit due to a serious crash; the ADS issues a request to intervene. The in-vehicle fallback-ready user becomes a driver and performs the fallback by manually operating the vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: in-vehicle user
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: user occupying a seat in the vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: lateral vehicle motion control
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The DDT subtask comprising the activities necessary for the real-time, sustained regulation of the y-axis component of vehicle motion (see Figure 9).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: longitudinal vehicle motion control
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The DDT subtask comprising the activities necessary for the real-time, sustained regulation of the x-axis component of vehicle motion (see Figure 9).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: low-volume traffic
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: traffic with a volume of less than 400 AADT (Annual Average Daily Traffic)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: maneuver-based feature
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: driving automation system feature equipped on a conventional vehicle that executes a limited set of lateral and/or longitudinal vehicle motion control actions (levels 1-4) as well as associated object and event detection and response (OEDR) and all other elements of the complete DDT (level 3 or 4) in order to fulfil a specific, narrowly defined use case (e.g., parking maneuver)

annotations.example: A Level 1 parking assistance feature automatically performs the lateral vehicle motion control actions necessary to parallel park a vehicle, while the driver performs the longitudinal vehicle motion control actions and supervises the feature.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: military base
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: facility for the storage of military equipment and the training of soldiers

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: military base, speed limit 25 kph, daylight
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: geographically-defined military base, only during daylight at speeds not to exceed 25 mph

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: minimal risk condition
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A stable, stopped condition to which a user or an ADS may bring a vehicle after performing the DDT fallback in order to reduce the risk of a crash when a given trip cannot or should not be continued.

annotations.example: A Level 4 ADS feature designed to operate a vehicle at high speeds on freeways experiences a DDT performance-relevant system failure and automatically removes the vehicle from active lanes of traffic before coming to a stop.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: monitor
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A general term describing a range of functions involving real-time human or machine sensing and processing of data used to operate a vehicle, or to support its operation.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: monitor driving automation system performance
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The activities and/or automated routines for evaluating whether the driving automation system is performing part or all of the DDT appropriately.

annotations.example: A remote driver engaging a Level 2 automated parking feature monitors the pathway of the vehicle to verify that the feature is responsive to pedestrians and obstacles.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: monitor the user
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The activities and/or automated routines designed to assess whether and to what degree the user is performing the role specified for him/her.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: monitor vehicle performance
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The activities and/or automated routines that accomplish real-time evaluation of the vehicle performance, and response preparation, as needed to operate a vehicle.

annotations.example: While a Level 2 driver support feature is engaged in stop-and-go traffic, a malfunctioning brake caliper causes the vehicle to pull slightly to the left when the brakes are applied. The human driver observes that the vehicle is deviating from its lane and either corrects the vehicle’s lateral position or disengages the feature entirely.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: monitor the driving environment
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The activities and/or automated routines that accomplish real-time roadway environmental object and event detection, recognition, classification, and response preparation (excluding actual response), as needed to operate a vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: motor vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: machine designed to provide conveyance on public streets, roads, and highways

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: motor vehicle operation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Collectively, the activities performed by a (human) driver (with or without support from one or more Level 1 or 2 driving automation features) or by an ADS (Level 3 to 5) to perform the entire DDT for a given vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: nighttime
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: period when there is no natural light from the sun

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: no driving automation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The performance by the driver of the entire DDT, even when enhanced by active safety systems.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: object and event detection and response
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The subtasks of the DDT that include monitoring the driving environment (detecting, recognizing, and classifying objects and events and preparing to respond as needed) and executing an appropriate response to such objects and events (i.e., as needed to complete the DDT and/or DDT fallback).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: operating condition
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: condition defining an operational design domain (ODD)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: operation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: act, process, or manner of operating

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: operation with driver
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: operation of a vehicle in which a human driver is present

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: operational design domain
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Operating conditions under which a given driving automation system or feature thereof is specifically designed to function, including, but not limited to, environmental, geographical, and time-of-day restrictions, and/or the requisite presence or absence of certain traffic or roadway characteristics.

annotations.example: A Level 1 ACC driver support feature is designed to provide longitudinal vehicle motion control support to the driver on fully access-controlled freeways under fair weather conditions.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: operational design domain exit
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: leaving the operational dessing domain (ODD) assigned to a specific function of the vehicle's ADS system

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: optimal road maintenance
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: road maintenance that guarantees a high level of comfort and convenience for users, which usually means roads that are two-lane, paved, with good lane markings and are not under construction

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: parking space
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: area where vehicles can be left

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: partial driving automation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The sustained and ODD-specific execution by a driving automation system of both the lateral and longitudinal vehicle motion control subtasks of the DDT with the expectation that the driver completes the OEDR subtask and supervises the driving automation system.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: passenger
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: user in a vehicle who has no role in the operation of that vehicle

annotations.example: The in-vehicle users of a Level 5 ADS-equipped dual-mode vehicle are passengers whenever the Level 5 ADS is engaged.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: predefined route
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: precisely defined route within a confined geographical area

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: remote assistance
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: event-driven provision, by a remotely located human (see 3.31.5), of information or advice to an ADS-equipped vehicle in driverless operation in order to facilitate trip continuation when the ADS encounters a situation it cannot manage

annotations.example: A Level 4 ADS-DV detects an object in its lane that appears to be too large to drive over and stops. A remote assistant uses the vehicle’s cameras to identify that the object is an empty bag that can be safely driven through/over, and provides the instruction to the ADS-DV to proceed.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: remote assistant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: human(s) who provides remote assistance to an ADS-equipped vehicle in driverless operation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: remote driver
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: driver who is not seated in a position to manually exercise in-vehicle braking, accelerating, steering, and transmission gear selection input devices (if any), but is able to operate the vehicle

annotations.example: A Level 2 automated parking feature allows the remote driver to exit the vehicle near an intended parking space and to cause the vehicle to move into the parking space automatically by pressing and holding a special button on the key fob, while s/he is monitoring the driving environment to ensure that no one and nothing enters the vehicle pathway during the parking maneuver. If, during the maneuver, a dog enters the pathway of the vehicle, the remote driver releases the button on the key fob in order to cause the vehicle to stop automatically. (Note that the remote driver in this Level 2 example completes the OEDR subtask of the DDT during the parking maneuver.)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: remote driving
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: real-time performance of part or all of the DDT and/or DDT fallback (including, real-time braking, steering, acceleration, and transmission shifting), by a remote driver

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: remote DDT fallback-ready user
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: fallback-ready user of a Level 3 ADS-equipped vehicle in driverless operation who is not in the driver’s seat

annotations.example: A Level 3 ADS-DV encounters a crash scene for which emergency personnel are re-routing traffic; the ADS issues a request to intervene. The remote fallback-ready user becomes a remote driver and performs the fallback by remotely operating the vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: request to intervene
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An alert provided by a Level 3 ADS to a fallback-ready user indicating that s/he should promptly perform the DDT fallback, which may entail resuming manual operation of the vehicle (i.e., becoming a driver again), or achieving a minimal risk condition if the vehicle is not operable.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: residental community area
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: area belonging to a residential community

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: road maintenance
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: preserving and keeping each type of roadway, roadside, structures as nearly as possible in its original condition as constructed or as subsequently improved and the operation of roadway facilities and services to provide satisfactory and safe transportation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: road type
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: particular kind of road

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: routine ADS operation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: operation of a vehicle by an ADS within its prescribed ODD, if any, while no DDT performance-relevant system failure is occurring

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: speed limit at which an ADS feature is designed to operate

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit 25
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: speed limit of 25 km per hour

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit 30
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: speed limit of 30 km per hour

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit 40
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: speed limit of 40 km per hour

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit 50
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: speed limit of 50 km per hour

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit 60
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: speed limit of 60 km per hour

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit 70
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: speed limit of 70 km per hour

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit 80
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: speed limit of 80 km per hour

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: stop-and-go traffic
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: phenomenon that highway vehicles, instead of maintaining a steady speed, are often forced to be engaged in repeated deceleration–acceleration cycles

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: sub-trip feature
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: driving automation system feature equipped on a conventional vehicle that requires a human driver to perform the complete DDT for at least part of every trip

annotations.example: A Level 1 adaptive cruise control (ACC) feature performs longitudinal vehicle motion control functions to support the driver in maintaining consistent headway to a lead vehicle in its lane when travelling at higher speeds.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: supervise DAS performance
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The driver activities, performed while operating a vehicle with an engaged Level 1 or 2 driver support feature, to monitor that feature’s performance, respond to inappropriate actions taken by the feature, and to otherwise complete the DDT.

annotations.example: A driver notices that an engaged adaptive cruise control (ACC) feature is not maintaining headway to a preceding vehicle in a curve and brakes accordingly.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: sustained operation of a vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Performance of part or all of the DDT both between and across external events, including responding to external events and continuing performance of part or all of the DDT in the absence of external events.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: time of day
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: particular time of day

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: traffic type
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: type of road traffic

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: trip
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The traversal of an entire travel pathway by a vehicle from the point of origin to a destination.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: university campus
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: land on which a college or university and related institutional buildings are situated

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: weather type
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: type of weather

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: task
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: function that a human or an automated driver can perform

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: land vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A transport vehicle which is neither an aircraft nor a watercraft.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: vehicle part
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: article the primary use of which is to improve, repair, replace, or serve as a component part of a vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: acceleration
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: increase in the speed of something

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: backward collision warning
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: notice of a possible collision with an object behind the vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: collision warning
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: notice of a possible collision

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: constant speed
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: value representing the speed of a vehicle and indicating that the speed is constant

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: deceleration
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: decrease in the speed of something

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: destination selection
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: decision where to go

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: driving action
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action which consists of the driver controlling and guiding the movement of a vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: dynamic driving task
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: all of the real-time operational and tactical functions required to operate a vehicle in on-road traffic, excluding the strategic functions

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: dynamic driving task subtask
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: specific real-time tactical or operational function required to operate a vehicle in on-road traffic

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: enhancing conspicuity
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: DDT subtask comprising activities which make the vehicle more visible and distinguishable from its surroundings, such as by lightning, sounding the horn, gesturing etc.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: forward collision warning
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: notice of a possible collision with an object in front of the vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: go
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action resulting in the vehicle changing its position

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: go backward
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action resulting in the vehicle moving backwards

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: go forward
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action resulting in the vehicle moving forward

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: green go
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: color of the traffic signal, evoked by light with a dominant wavelength of roughly 495-570 nm that signalizes that vehicle is allowed to and should go forward

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: lane change
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action during which the vehicle changes lanes

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: lane departure warning
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: notice of the departure from the lane

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: lateral vehicle motion control
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: the DDT subtask comprising the activities necessary for the real-time, sustained regulation of the y-axis component of vehicle motion

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: left lane change
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action during which a vehicle changes lanes, moving to the one on the left

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: longitudinal vehicle motion control
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: the DDT subtask comprising the activities necessary for the real-time, sustained regulation of the x-axis component of vehicle motion

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: maneuver planning
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: function that includes deciding whether and when to overtake another vehicle or change lanes

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: monitor
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a range of functions involving real-time human or machine sensing and processing of data used to operate a vehicle, or to support its operation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: monitor driving automation system performance
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: the activities automated routines for evaluating whether the driving automation system is performing part or all of the DDT appropriately

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: monitor the driving environment
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: the activities automated routines that accomplish real-time roadway environmental object and event detection, recognition, classification, and response preparation (excluding actual response), as needed to operate a vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: monitor the user
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: the activities and/or automated routines designed to assess whether and to what degree the user is performing the role specified for him/her

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: monitor vehicle performance for DDT performance-relevant system failures
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: the activities and/or automated routines that accomplish real-time evaluation of the vehicle performance, and response preparation, as needed to operate a vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: object and event detection and response
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: the subtasks of the DDT that include monitoring the driving environment (detecting, recognizing, and classifying objects and events and preparing to respond as needed) and executing an appropriate response to such objects and events (i.e., as needed to complete the DDT and/or DDT fallback)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: operate a motor vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: the activities performed by a (human) driver (with or without support from one or more level 1 or 2 driving automation features ) or by an ADS (level 3-5) to perform the entire DDT for a given vehicle during a trip

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: operational effort
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a function that involves split-second reactions that can be considered pre-cognitive or innate, such as making micro-corrections to steering, braking and accelerating to maintain lane position in traffic or to avoid a sudden obstacle or hazardous event in the vehicle’s pathway

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: overspeed warning
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: notice that the speed of a vehicle is above the legally determined value

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: red stop
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: color of a traffic signal, evoked by light with a dominant wavelength of roughly 625-740 nm, which indicates that the vehicle is not allowed to go forward and should stop

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: right lane change
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action during which a vehicle changes lanes, moving to the one on the right

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: road condition
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: structured value representing the current condition of a road

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: side collision warning
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: notice of a possible collision with an object located at the side of the vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: smooth acceleration
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: gradual increase in the speed of a vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: smooth deceleration
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: gradual decrease in the speed of a vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed profile
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: juxtaposition of all changes in the speed of a vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: stop
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action resulting in the vehicle stopping any movement

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: strategic function
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: function that involves deciding whether, where and when to go, how to travel, which best routes to take, etc.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: sudden acceleration
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: sudden increase in the speed of a vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: sudden deceleration
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: sudden decrease in the speed of a vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: tactical effort
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a function that involves maneuvering the vehicle in traffic during a trip, including deciding whether and when to overtake another vehicle or change lanes, selecting an appropriate speed, checking mirrors, etc

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: to left
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action resulting in the vehicle making a below 90 degrees turn to the left

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: to right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action resulting in the vehicle making a below 90 degrees turn to the right

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: traffic signal control
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: highway traffic signal by which traffic is alternately directed to stop and permitted to proceed

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: trip scheduling
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: decision when to go

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: turn left
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action resulting in the vehicle making an above, or equal to 90 degrees turn to the left

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: turn right
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action resulting in the vehicle making an above, or equal to 90 degrees turn to the right

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: wait then go
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action that consists of the vehicle firstly not moving, and then moving

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: warning
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: notice of possible danger or a problem

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: waypoint selection
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: selection of a waypoint

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: yellow
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: color of a traffic signal, evoked by light with a dominant wavelength of roughly 575-585 nm which is an intermediate between red and green

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: airport
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: place from which aircraft operate that usually has paved runways and maintenance facilities and often serves as a terminal

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: airway
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A transport way reserved primarily for use by aircraft taking off, in flight, or landing.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: amenity
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: something that helps to provide comfort, convenience, or enjoyment

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: at grade intersection
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An intersection where all roadways cross or join at the same level.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: auxiliary road sign
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: sign that provides information such as direction, time and temperature displays, hours of operation, or warning; auxiliary signs are intended for the convenience of the public. An auxiliary sign may include the business name and/or logo, but may not include its product or services

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: bank
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: establishment for the custody, loan, exchange, or issue of money, for the extension of credit, and for facilitating the transmission of funds

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: bicycle lane
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A bikeway adjacent to travel lanes which has been designated for preferential or exclusive use by pedalcyclists through striping, signage or pavement markings

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: bicycle trail
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A bikeway reserved for pedalcycles and separated from roadways by open space or barriers.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: bikeway
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A trafficway specifically designated as being open for pedalcycle travel or, where various classes of pedalcycle are segregated, that part of a trafficway open for a particular class (See 2.2.28)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: building
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: usually roofed and walled structure built for permanent use

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: bus lane
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: part of the road which is intended to be used only by buses

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: bus station
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: place incorporating waiting areas, stands for buses, and ticket offices from which buses or coaches depart

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: bus stop
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: place on a road where buses stop to let passengers on and off

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: business district
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: territory contiguous to and including a highway when within any 600 feet along such highway there are buildings in use for business or industrial purposes, including but not limited to hotels, banks, office buildings, railroad stations and public buildings which occupy at least 300 feet of frontage on one side or 300 feet collectively on both sides of the highway

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: channelized intersection
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An at-grade intersection in which traffic is diverted into definite paths by raised or painted traffic islands.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: city street
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A trafficway within a city trafficway system that is not an Interstate highway, other U.S. route numbered highway, other state route numbered highway, or county road.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: college
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: institution offering instruction, usually in a professional, vocational, or technical field

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: convenience
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: small, often franchised market that is open long hours

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: county road
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A trafficway within a county trafficway system that is not an Interstate highway, other U.S. route numbered highway, or other state route numbered highway.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: crosswalk
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: (1) that part of a roadway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks on opposite sides of the roadway measured from the curbs or, in the absence of curbs, from the edges of the traversable roadway, or (2) any portion of a roadway at an intersection or elsewhere distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface of the roadway.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: crosswalk road segment
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: road segment which contains a crosswalk

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: curb return
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The curved section of curb used at intersections in joining straight sections of curb.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: directional road sign
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: sign installed on public land that advertises the direction to be taken to a service, tourist attraction or a townsite/locality

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: driveway
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A private way which provides vehicular access to the public from a trafficway to property, parking or loading areas outside the boundaries of the trafficway, but is considered to be not open to the public for transportation purposes as a trafficway.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: driveway access
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A portion of the trafficway at the end of a driveway (See 2.5.9.1), providing access to property adjacent to a trafficway.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: educational institute
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: institute that provides education as its main purpose

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: end lane
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: lane located at the end of a path

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: end node
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: end GPS position of a path

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: fast food
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: restaurant specializing in food that can be prepared and served quickly

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: fire station
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: building housing fire apparatus and usually firefighters

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: forest
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: dense growth of trees and underbrush covering a large tract

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: frontage road
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A roadway generally paralleling an expressway, freeway, parkway or through street so designed as to intercept, collect and distribute traffic desiring to cross, enter or leave such facility and to furnish access to property which otherwise would be isolated as a result of controlled-access features.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: fully-controlled access highway
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A trafficway on which preference is given to through traffic by permitting access only from other trafficways and by providing grade separations at all crossing trafficways.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: gas station
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: retail station for servicing motor vehicles, especially with gasoline and oil

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: gore
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An area of land where two roadways diverge or converge.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: grade separation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A crossing at different levels of two trafficways, or a trafficway and a railway.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: highway
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: road that is part of the strategic traffic network for automobiles across the country and connects areas of political/economic importance or areas that are critical to the nation's interests

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: hospital
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: institution where the sick or injured are given medical or surgical care

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: infrastructure
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: basic installations and facilities on which the continuance and growth of a community, state, etc. depend, such as roads, schools, power plants, transportation and communication systems, etc.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: instruction road sign
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: sign which does not contain advertising or promotional matter but relates solely to traffic or pedestrian control, warnings or hours of operation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: instruction surface sign
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: sign which does not contain advertising or promotional matter but relates solely to traffic or pedestrian control, warnings or hours of operation, that is located on the road surface

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: interchange
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A system of interconnecting roadways in conjunction with one or more grade separations, providing for the movement of traffic between two or more roadways on different levels.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: intersection
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An area which (1) contains a crossing or connection of two or more roadways not classified as driveway access and (2) is embraced within the prolongation of the lateral curb lines or, if none, the lateral boundary lines of the roadways.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: intersection segment
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: path segment that contains an intersection of two or more lanes

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: interstate highway
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A trafficway on the Interstate System.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: interstate system
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The National System of Interstate and Defense Highways as defined in Section 101, Title 23, United States Code.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: junction
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An intersection or the connection between a driveway access and a roadway other than a driveway access.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: kindergarten
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: school or class for children usually from four to six years old

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: lake
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: considerable inland body of standing water

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: land way
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The space within property lines or other boundary lines of any transport way that is neither an airway nor a waterway.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: lane
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: one of the longitudinal strips into which the carriageway is divisible, whether or not defined by longitudinal road markings, which is wide enough for one moving line of motor vehicles other than motorcycles

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: lane adapter
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: connection between an uncontrolled intersection and a two-way narrow road

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: leisure
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: large public building containing different facilities for leisure activities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: longitudinal part of trafficway
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: part of a traffic way which is a roadway or a line parallel to it

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: median
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An area of a trafficway between parallel roads separating travel in opposite directions.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: metro station
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: station for a rapid transit system, which as a whole is usually called a "metro" or "subway"

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: municipal road
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: road that is part of the road network within municipal jurisdiction

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: national road
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: road that is part of the strategic road network for the nation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: natural place
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: place created by nature to which people come for entertainment

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: node
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: single point in space defined by its latitude, longitude and node ID

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: one way lane
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: lane where driving vehicles otherwise than in one direction is prohibited

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: ordinary road
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: road that is not a highway

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: other sign
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: other sign that can be encountered by the driver on the road

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: other state route numbered highway
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A trafficway within a state trafficway system, but not an interstate highway or other U.S. route numbered highway.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: other US route numbered highway another
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A trafficway numbered by the American Association of State Highway Officials, but not an interstate highway.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: park
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: piece of ground in or near a city or town kept for ornament and recreation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: parking lot
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An area used primarily for parking road vehicles.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: parking lot way
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A parking lots open to the public are trafficways.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: parking place
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: place to park a car, truck, etc

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: path
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: line of movement of a vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: path segment
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: part of a path that can be an intersection, a lane, a crosswalk or a turn

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: pharmacy
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: place where medicines are compounded or dispensed

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: police station
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: headquarters of the police for a locality

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: post office
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: local branch of a national post office handling the mail for a particular place or area

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: prefectural road
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: road that is part of the regional arterial road network

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: private road
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: road owned by a private entity

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: private way
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any land way other than a trafficway.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: railway
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any private way reserved primarily for land vehicles moving persons or property from one place to another on rails.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: railway station
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: building containing accommodations for railroad passengers or freight

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: ramp
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An auxiliary roadway used for entering or leaving through-traffic lanes.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: regulatory road sign
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: sign used to inform road users of selected traffic laws or regulations and indicate the applicability of the legal requirements

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: regulatory surface sign
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: sign used to inform road users of selected traffic laws or regulations and indicate the applicability of the legal requirements located on the road surface

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: residential district
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: territory contiguous to and including a highway not comprising a business district when the property on such highway for a distance of 300 feet or more is in the main improved with residences or residences and buildings in use for business

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: restaurant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: business establishment where meals or refreshments may be purchased

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: river
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: natural stream of water of usually considerable volume

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: road
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A part of a trafficway which includes both the roadway and any shoulder alongside the roadway.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: road part
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: part of the road

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: road segment
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: segment of the road

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: road sign
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: sign located on or visible from the road that informs the drivers about laws, attractions, regulations and more

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: road surface marking
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: marking located on the road surface, which informs the drivers about laws, attractions, regulations and more

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: road type
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: particular kind of road

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: roadside
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The outermost part of the trafficway from the property line or other boundary in to the edge of the first road.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: roadway
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A part of a trafficway designed, improved and ordinarily used for motor vehicle travel or, where various classes of motor vehicles are segregated, that part of a trafficway used by a particular class.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: roundabout
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: circular intersection with yield control at entry, which permits a vehicle on the circulatory roadway to proceed, and with deflection of the approaching vehicle counter-clockwise around a central island

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: school
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: institution for the teaching of children

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: separator
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The area of a trafficway between parallel roads separating travel in the same direction or separating a frontage road (See 2.5.18) from other roads.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: shared road
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any bikeway which is part of a roadway, but not a bicycle lane.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: shop
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: small retail establishment or a department in a large one offering a specified line of goods or services

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: shoulder
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A part of a trafficway contiguous with the roadway for emergency use, for accommodation of stopped road vehicles, and for lateral support of the roadway structure.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: maximum (or minimum) speed applicable to a section of highway as established by law or regulation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit 100
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: speed limit of 100 km per hour

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit 25
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: speed limit of 25 km per hour

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit 30
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: speed limit of 30 km per hour

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit 40
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: speed limit of 40 km per hour

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit 50
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: speed limit of 50 km per hour

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit 60
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: speed limit of 60 km per hour

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit 70
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: speed limit of 70 km per hour

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed limit 80
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: speed limit of 80 km per hour

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: sports centre
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: place where people take part in sports

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: start lane
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: lane located at the start of a path

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: start node
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: starting GPS position of a path

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: station
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: regular stopping place on a transportation route

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: supermarket
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: self-service retail market selling especially foods and household merchandise

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: toll gate
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: point where the driver of a vehicle must pay a toll

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: traffic sign
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: road sign, signal, device, notice or road marking that identifies a danger, advises persons of the precautions to be taken against such danger, indicates the existence of a road regulation or implements such a regulation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: traffic signal
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: device manually, electrically or mechanically operated for the regulation of traffic

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: trafficway
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any land way open to the public as a matter of right or custom for moving persons or property from one place to another.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: transport way
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any way or place reserved or commonly used for the operation of transport vehicles.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: turn
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: instant change of direction of a singular road

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: turn lane
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A lane exclusively designated for vehicles turning from one trafficway to another.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: two way lane
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: lane allowing for two-way traffic

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: university
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: institution of higher learning providing facilities for teaching and research and authorized to grant academic degrees

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: urban area
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An area whose boundaries shall be those fixed by responsible state and local officials in cooperation with each other and approved by the Federal Highway Administration, U.S. Department of Transportation.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: urban district
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: territory contiguous to and including any street built up with structures devoted to business, industry or dwelling houses situated at intervals of less than 100 feet for a distance of a quarter of a mile or more

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: utility pole
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: tall pole that is used to support telephone wires, electrical wires, etc

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: warning road sign
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: sign used to indicate conditions that are actually or potentially hazardous to users of the road

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: waterway
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A transport way reserved primarily for use by watercraft.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: work zone
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An area of a trafficway where construction, maintenance or utility work activities are identified by warning signs/signals/indicators, including those on transport devices (e.g., signs, flashing lights, channelizing devices, barriers, pavement markings, flagmen, warning signs and arrow boards mounted on the vehicles in a mobile maintenance activity) that mark the beginning and end of a construction, maintenance or utility work activity.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: accident
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: something bad that happens that is not expected or intended and that often damages something or injures someone

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: aircraft accident
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A transport accident that involves an aircraft in-transport.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: at-intersection crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A traffic crash in which the first harmful event occurs within the limits of an intersection.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: at work
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Engaged in duties, activities or tasks that produce a product or service; that are done in exchange for money, goods, services, profit or benefit; and that are legal activities in the United States.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: cataclysm
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An avalanche, landslide/mudslide, hurricane, cyclone, downburst, flood, torrential rain, cloudburst, lightning, tornado, tidal wave, earthquake or volcanic eruption (See 2.4.9 transport crash).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: collision
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: occurs when a vehicle that is moving along a roadway collides with another vehicle or object

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: collision crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A road vehicle crash other than an overturning crash in which the first harmful event is a collision of a road vehicle in-transport with another road vehicle, other property or pedestrians.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: collision involving motor vehicle in-transport
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A crash that is both a motor vehicle crash and a collision crash in which the first harmful event is the collision of two or more motor vehicles in-transport.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: collision involving other road vehicle in transport
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A crash that is both an other-road vehicle crash and a collision crash in which the first harmful event is the collision of two or more other road vehicles in-transport.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: collision involving animal
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A collision crash in which the first harmful event is the collision of an animal, other than an animal powering an other road vehicle, and a road vehicle in-transport.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: collision involving fixed object
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A collision crash in which the first harmful event is the striking of a fixed object by a road vehicle in- transport.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: collision involving other object
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any collision crash other than a (1) collision involving pedestrian, (2) collision involving motor vehicle in-transport, (3) collision involving other road vehicle in-transport, (4) collision involving parked motor vehicle, (5) collision involving railway vehicle, (6) collision involving pedalcycle, (7) collision involving animal, or (8) collision involving fixed object.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: collision involving other road vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A collision involving other road vehicle in- in Transport transport is a crash that is both an other-road- vehicle crash and a collision crash in which the first harmful event is the collision of two or more other road vehicles in-transport.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: collision involving parked motor
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A crash in which the first harmful event is the striking of a motor vehicle not in- transport (See 2.2.34.1) by a road vehicle in- transport (See 2.2.34).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: collision involving pedalcycle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A crash that is both a motor vehicle crash and a collision crash in which the first harmful event is the collision of a pedalcycle in-transport and a motor vehicle in- transport.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: collision involving pedestrian crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A collision crash in which the first harmful event is the collision of a pedestrian and a road vehicle in- transport.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: collision involving railway vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A collision crash in which the first harmful event is the collision of a road vehicle in-transport and a railway vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: commerce
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any trade, traffic or transportation of commodities or persons for financial consideration or exchange, or in the furtherance of a business enterprise.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: contact vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any road vehicle which comes in contact with one or more road vehicles, non-motorists or property in a collision crash, or has a noncollision crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An unstabilized situation which includes at least one harmful event.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: damage
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A harm to property that reduces the monetary value of that property.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: dangerous behaviour
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action by a traffic user which results in a traffic incident

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: dangerous overtaking
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action in which a traffic user overtakes another vehicle in a way that leads to an incident

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: death
