https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a process leading to the cessation of all vital functions of the body as a result of irreversible inhibition of biological reactions in its cells

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: deliberate intent
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The classification given to the cause of an event which occurs when a person acts deliberately to cause the event or deliberately refrains from prudent acts which would prevent occurrence of the event.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: destruction of property
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: damage to or the destruction of public or private property, caused either by a person who is not its owner or by natural phenomena

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: disabling damage
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A road vehicle damage which precludes departure of the vehicle from the scene of the crash in its usual operating manner by daylight after simple repairs.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: driver
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An occupant who is in actual physical control of a transport vehicle or, for an out-of control vehicle, an occupant who was in control until control was lost.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: driveway access-related crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A traffic crash that (1) occurs adjacent to a driveway, (2) is not a driveway access crash and (3) results from an activity, behavior or control related to the movement of traffic units onto or out of a driveway.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: driveway-towaway operation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: operation in which an empty or unladen motor vehicle with one or more sets of wheels on the surface of the roadway is being transported by means of a saddle-mount or tow-bar between vehicle manufacturer's facilities, a vehicle manufacturer and a dealership or purchaser or to a repair facility

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: driveway access crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A traffic crash in which the first harmful event occurs on a driveway access (See 2.5.9) or involves a road vehicle entering or leaving another roadway by way of a driveway access (See Figure 4).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: driving under the influence
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: driving motor or non-mechanical vehicles during or after consuming alcohol or psychoactive substances

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: entrance/exit ramp-related crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A traffic crash in which the first harmful event occurs off the entrance/exit ramp roadway, but is related to the use of or entry onto the ramp.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: entrance/exit ramp crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A traffic crash in which the first harmful event occurs on an entrance or exit ramp roadway and is not the result of an activity, behavior or control related to the movement of traffic units through an intersection.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: entry on red light
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action of crossing the pedestrian crossing while the traffic light is red

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: fainting
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: krótkotrwała utrata przytomności wywołana przejściowym globalnym zmniejszeniem perfuzji mózgowej. Charakteryzuje się szybkim rozwojem objawów aż do zupełnej utraty przytomności, krótkim czasem trwania oraz samoistnym i pełnym odzyskaniem przytomności.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: farm vehicle driver
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: farmer who drives a commercial motor vehicle that is used within 150 air-miles of their farm to transport agricultural products, farm machinery, farm supplies, or both, to or from a farm

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: fatal crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any injury crash that results in one or more fatal injuries.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: fatal injury
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any injury that results in death within 30 days after the motor vehicle crash in which the injury occurred.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: fatality
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any death resulting from a fatal injury.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: forcing the right of way
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: niepowstrzymanie się od ruchu, jeżeli ruch mógłby zmusić innego kierującego do zmiany kierunku lub pasa ruchu albo istotnej zmiany prędkości, a pieszego - do zatrzymania się, zwolnienia lub przyspieszenia kroku

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: functional damage
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any road vehicle damage, other than disabling damage, which affects operation of the road vehicle or its parts.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: harmful event
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An occurrence of injury or damage.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: hazardous material
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A substance or material which has been designated by the U.S. Department of Transportation, or other authorizing entity, as capable of posing an unreasonable risk to health, safety and property when transported in commerce.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: hazardous materials placard
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A sign required to be affixed to any motor vehicle transporting quantities of hazardous materials in quantities above the thresholds established by the U.S. Department of Transportation, or other authorized entity.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: in-transport
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The state or condition of a transport vehicle which is in motion or within the portion of a transport way ordinarily used by similar transport vehicles.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: injury
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A bodily harm to a person.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: injury crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any road vehicle crash that results in one or more injuries.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: inoperative vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: state of a vehicle in which some or all of its functions do not work

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: interchange crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A traffic crash in which the first harmful event occurs within boundaries which include all ramps of auxiliary roadways and include each roadway entering or leaving the interchange to a point 30 meters (100 feet) beyond the gore or curb return at the outermost ramp connection. Interchange crashes may include at-intersection crashes, intersection- related crashes, driveway access crashes or nonjunction crashes.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: intersection-related crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A traffic crash in which the first harmful event (1) occurs on an approach to or exit from an intersection and (2) results from an activity, behavior or control related to the movement of traffic units through the intersection.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: interstate commerce
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A commerce in the United States where the transit between the points of origin and termination does not occur entirely within the borders of the state of origin.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: interstate system
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The National System of Interstate and Defense Highways as defined in Section 101, Title 23, United States Code.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: intrastate commerce
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A commerce in any state where the transit between the points of origin and termination occurs entirely within the borders of the state of origin.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: jackknife crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A noncollision crash in which the first harmful event results from unintended contact between any two units of a multi-unit road vehicle such as a truck combination.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: legal intervention
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A category of deliberate intent in which the person who acts or refrains from acting is a law-enforcing agent or other official.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: motor carrier
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The legal business entity, individual, partnership, corporation or organization that directs, controls and is responsible for the transportation of goods, property or people.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: motor vehicle crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A transport crash that (1) involves a motor vehicle in-transport, (2) is not an aircraft accident or watercraft accident, and (3) does not include any harmful event involving a railway train in-transport prior to involvement of a motor vehicle in-transport.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: motor vehicle damage
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A road vehicle damage to a motor vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: motor vehicle nontraffic crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A motor vehicle crash which is a nontraffic crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: motor vehicle traffic crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A motor vehicle cash which is a traffic crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: motorcycle conversion kit
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A device that makes it possible to convert a conventional two-wheel motorcycle into a motorcycle having the look and the stability of a tricycle-type vehicle, which improves stability and increases ease of operation.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: motorist
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any occupant of a motor vehicle in-transport.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: moving object
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: object which is in motion and changes location

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: no apparent injury (O)
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A situation where there is no reason to believe that the person received any bodily harm from the motor vehicle crash. There is no physical evidence of injury and the person does not report any change in normal function.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: no apparent injury crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any road vehicle crash other than an injury crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: non-contact vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any vehicle other than a contact vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: non-fatal injury crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any injury crash other than a fatal crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: non-junction crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A road vehicle crash that is not an at-intersection crash, a driveway access crash or an intersection-related crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: non-motorist
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any person other than a motorist

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: non-traffic crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A road vehicle crash which is not a traffic crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: noncollision crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any road vehicle crash other than a collision crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: niedostosowanie prędkości do warunków atmosferycznych
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action of driving at a speed that is inadequate to weather conditions

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: not in-transport
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The state or condition of a transport vehicle which is not "in-transport."

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: occupant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any person who is part of a transport vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: off-roadway crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any road vehicle crash other than an on-roadway crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: on-roadway crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: (1) a collision crash in which the initial point of contact between colliding units in the first harmful event is within a roadway or (2) a non-collision crash in which the road vehicle involved was partly or entirely on the roadway at the time of the first harmful event.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: other-road-vehicle crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A transport crash that (1) involves an other road vehicle in- transport and (2) is not an aircraft accident, watercraft accident, motor vehicle crash or railway accident.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: other-road-vehicle damage
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A road vehicle damage to an other road vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: other-road-vehicle nontraffic crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An other-road-vehicle crash which is a nontraffic crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: other-road-vehicle traffic crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An other- road-vehicle crash which is a traffic crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: inne przedmioty z którymi samochód może się zderzyć
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: objects other than infrastructure, agents, vehicles, property, natural places, hazardous material, hazardous material placard, with which vehicles can collide

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: overturning crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A road vehicle crash in which the first harmful event is the overturning of a road vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: passenger
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any occupant of a road vehicle other than its driver.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: pedalcycle crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An other-road-vehicle crash that (1) involves a pedalcycle in-transport and (2) is not a streetcar crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: pedalcyclist
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any occupant of a pedalcycle in-transport.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: pedestrian
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any person who is not an occupant.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: personal conveyance
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A device, other than a transport device, used by a pedestrian (See 2.2.36) for personal mobility assistance or recreation. These devices can be motorized or human powered, but not propelled by pedaling.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: police pursuit
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An event that is initiated when a law enforcement officer, operating an authorized emergency vehicle, gives notice to stop to a motorist the officer is attempting to contact, and that motorist fails to comply with the signal by either maintaining his/her speed, increasing speed, or taking other evasive action to elude the officer 's continued attempts to stop the motorist.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: possible injury
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any injury reported or claimed which is not a fatal, suspected serious, or suspected minor injury.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: private motor carrier
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: person who provides transportation of property or passengers, by commercial motor vehicle, and is not a for-hire motor carrier

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: property
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any physical object other than a person.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: property damage only crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A no apparent injury crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: qualified VA examiner
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: advanced practice nurse, doctor of chiropractic, doctor of medicine, doctor of osteopathy, physician assistant, or other medical professional who is employed in the Department of Veterans Affairs

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: radar detector
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: device or mechanism designed to detect the emission of radio microwaves, laser beams or any other future speed measurement technology employed by enforcement personnel to measure the speed of commercial motor vehicles upon public roads and highways for enforcement purposes

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: railway accident
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A transport accident that (1) involves a railway train in-transport and (2) is not an aircraft accident, watercraft accident or motor vehicle crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: receiver
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: person who takes delivery from a motor carrier or driver of a commercial motor vehicle of property transported in interstate commerce or hazardous materials transported in interstate or intrastate commerce

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: road vehicle crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A transport crash that is either a motor vehicle crash or an other-road vehicle crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: road vehicle damage
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A damage to a road vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: road vehicle nontraffic crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A nontraffic crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: road vehicle traffic crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A traffic crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: role in accident
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: role a vehicle takes in an accident

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: role of person in traffic
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: role a person can take while being in traffic

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: school bus crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: (1) a motor vehicle crash in which a school bus, with or without a pupil on board, is involved directly as a contact vehicle, or (2) a motor vehicle crash or an other-road- vehicle crash in which a school bus, with or without a pupil on board, is involved indirectly as a noncontact vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: niedopasowanie prędkości
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action of having inadequate speed

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: state
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: state or condition of a transport vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: obiekt statyczny
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: object that does not move

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: streetcar crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: An other-road-vehicle crash that involves a streetcar in-transport.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: suspected minor injury
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any injury that is evident at the scene of the crash, other than fatal or serious injuries, including lump on the head, abrasions, bruises, minor lacerations (cuts on the skin surface with minimal bleeding and no exposure of deeper tissue /muscles).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: suspected serious injury
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any injury other than fatal which results in one or more of the following : Severe laceration resulting in exposure of underlying tissues /muscle /organs or resulting in significant loss of blood; broken or distorted extremity (arm or leg); crush injuries; suspected skull, chest, or abdominal injury other than bruises or minor lacerations; significant burns (second and third degree burns over 10 % or more of the body); unconsciousness when taken from the crash scene, or paralysis.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: too high
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action of having too high speed

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: too low
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action of having too low speed

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: too small distance between vehicles
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action of maintaining too small a distance between two vehicles

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: traffic crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A road vehicle crash in which (1) the unstabilized situation originates on a trafficway or (2) a harmful event occurs on a trafficway.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: traffic incident
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: all road accidents - irrespective of whether there is an accident or serious material damage

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: przyczyna zdarzeń drogowych
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: possible causes of a traffic incident

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: skutek zdarzeń drogowych
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: possible effect of a traffic incident

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: traffic participant
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: pedestrians, drivers, and other people in the vehicle or on a vehicle on the road

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: traffic unit
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A land vehicle or a pedestrian.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: traffic violation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: czyn społecznie szkodliwy (nawet w stopniu znikomym), zabroniony przez ustawę obowiązującą w czasie jego popełnienia pod groźbą kary aresztu, ograniczenia wolności, grzywny do 5000 złotych lub nagany

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: transport crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A crash (1) that involves a transport vehicle in-transport, (2) in which the first harmful event is not produced by the discharge of a firearm or explosive device, and (3) that does not directly result from a cataclysm where the timing is such that the cataclysm is occurring at the time of the accident or crash.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: transport device
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any device designed primarily for moving persons or property along with the device itself from one place to another, except (1) a weapon, (2) a device used primarily within the confines of a building and its premises, or (3) a personal conveyance.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: unstabilized situation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A set of events not under human control.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: korzystanie z telefonu komórkowego podczas prowadzenia samochodu
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: action of using a mobile phone by a driver while operating a vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: veteran operator
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: operator of a commercial motor vehicle who is a veteran enrolled in the health care system

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: poszkodowanie
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: to be hurt or damaged because of something or someone

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: watercraft accident
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A transport accident if it (1) involves a watercraft in-transport and (2) is not an aircraft accident.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: pogoda
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: current atmospheric conditions

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: work zone crash
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A motor vehicle traffic crash in which the first harmful event occurs within the boundaries of a work zone or on an approach to or exit from a work zone, resulting from an activity, behavior or control related to the movement of the traffic units through the work zone.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: QName: auto-mo-mo:Action

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: QName: auto-mo-mo:Agent

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: QName: auto-mo-mo:PostalAddress

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: process
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: QName: auto-mo-mo:Process

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: property value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A property-value pair, e.g. representing a feature of a product or place.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: qualitative value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a predefined value for a product characteristic, e.g. the power cord plug type 'US' or the garment sizes 'S', 'M', 'L', and 'XL'

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: quantitative value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a point value or interval for product characteristics and other purposes

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: quantitative value float
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: QName: auto-mo-mo:QuantitativeValueFloat

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: quantitative value integer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: QName: auto-mo-mo:QuantitativeValueInteger

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: QName: auto-mo-mo:Role

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: QName: auto-mo-mo:TextValue

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: agricultural commodity trailer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: trailer that is designed to transport bulk agricultural commodities in off-road harvesting sites and to a processing plant or storage location, as evidenced by skeletal construction that accommodates harvest containers, a maximum length of 28 feet, and an arrangement of air control lines and reservoirs that minimizes damage in field operations

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: aircraft
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A transport vehicle designed primarily for, or in use for, moving persons or property through the air from one place to another.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: audio and navigation choice or component
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The class of audio and navigation choices or components (CD/DVD/SatNav, a "MonoSelectGroup" in automotive terminology), VW ID: 1

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: autocycle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A large motorcycle with one rear wheel and two front wheels, with either a saddle and handlebars or seat (s) and a steering wheel, that can be fully enclosed, partially enclosed, or unenclosed.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: base model
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A Base Model is an abstract entity specifying the basic features of a group of vehicles. Examples: VW Golf, VW Polo, VW Passat

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: bicycle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a pedal-driven, human-powered, single-track vehicle, having two wheels attached to a frame, one behind the other. Some bicycles have a small combustion or electric engine that assists with the pedaling.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: boat
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a watercraft of modest size designed to float or plane, to provide passage across water

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: boat trailer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: trailer designed with cradle-type mountings to transport a boat and configured to permit the launching of the boat from the rear of the trailer

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: body style value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a value indicating the body style of a vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: autobus
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A motor vehicle with seating for transporting nine or more persons, including the driver.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: business entity
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: entity that is formed and administered as per commercial law in order to engage in business activities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: business entity type
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: type of a business entity

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: canoe
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a small narrow boat, typically human-powered, though it may also be powered by sails or small electric or gas motors

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: car
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A motor vehicle other than a motorcycle, utility vehicle or low speed vehicle consisting of a transport device typically designed for carrying eight or fewer persons.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: car usage
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a special usage of a car, e.g. commercial rental, driving school, or as a taxi

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: cargo van
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any van where the area behind the driver or cab is designed for transporting cargo or operated for general commercial use.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: charter bus
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A bus providing contract service for a group tour or outing, usually on a round-trip basis.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: check
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a mandatory or optional technical inspection, e.g. the MOT, a vendor-specific certification of used cars, etc.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: choice or component
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A Choice or Component is a component (e.g. engine), add-on, feature (color "ocean blue"), or service that can be chosen to be part of a final vehicle configuration. Example: Engine 1.6 l TDI, color ocean blue, trailer hitch

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: commercial motor vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any motor vehicle used for the transportation of goods, property or people in interstate (See 2.9.2) or intrastate (2.9.3) commerce.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: complete car model
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A Complete Car Model is an abstract entity specifying all features and configuration choices needed for actually producing a vehicle. In other words, it is the gr:ProductOrServiceModel ("datasheet") for a completely configured vehicle. While a Complete Car Model can be defined indepently of a Base Model, Trim, or Derivative, it is usually based on a Derivative plus choices for all mandatory configurational options (coo:SpecItemCollection) of that Derivative. A Complete Car Model should be linked to its Derivative via gr:isVariantOf, if available. Example: VW Golf S 1.6 TDI 3door Manual in ocean blue with air-conditioning, CD player, trailer hitch, power steering, and power windows Note: A coo:CompleteCarModel is NOT an actual car, but a complete feature description of one or multiple actual cars.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: configuration info
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A Configuration Info is an abstract entity that gives information on whether a set of Choices Or Components results in a valid configuration. Using coo:compatible, it is possible to indicate either compatibility (true) and incompatibility (false) so that modeling remains efficient, no matter whether most combinations are valid or whether most configurations are invalid. If no such statement is found, the validity of a configuration is unknown. Note: The two properties coo:includes and coo:dependsOn, attached to coo:ChoiceOrComponent, may contain additional information on the validity of configuration.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: container chassis trailer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: semitrailer of skeleton construction limited to a bottom frame, one or more axles, specially built and fitted with locking devices for the transport of intermodal cargo containers so that when the chassis and container are assembled, the units serve the same function as an over the road trailer

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: covered farm vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: straight truck or articulated vehicle that is registered in a State with a license plate or other designation issued by the State of registration that allows law enforcement officials to identify it as a farm vehicle and used to transport agricultural commodities, livestock, machinery or supplies to or from a farm or ranch

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: crib-type log trailer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: trailer equipped with stakes, bunks, a front-end structure, and a rear structure to restrain logs

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: damage or accident
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: an event in which the vehicle is being damaged

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: decorative trims choice or component
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The class of decorative trim choices or components (a "MonoSelectGroup" in automotive terminology), VW ID: 8

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: derivative
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A Derivative is an abstract entity specifying (1) the basic features plus (2) a set of functional (e.g. engine type) and non-functional configuration (e.g. upholstery) choices of a group of vehicles. A Derivative has often a number of remaining configuration choices (coo:SpecItemCollection attached via coo:hasSpecItems), which will determine the actual properties of the resulting vehicle. A Derivative should be linked to its Trim via gr:isVariantOf, if available. Examples: VW Golf S 1.6 TDI 3door Manual

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: drive wheel configuration value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a value indicating which roadwheels will receive torque

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: emission standard value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a value indicating the an emission standard

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: engine choice or component
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The class of engines as choices or components

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: engine specification
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: information about the engine of the vehicle. A vehicle can have multiple engines represented by multiple engine specification entities

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: engine type value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a value indicating an engine type

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: feature value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a value indicating the features or accessories that are attached to or belong to a vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: financing
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: the specification of a payment option via staged payments

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: fuel quantity
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a value indicating an amount of fuel

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: fuel type value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a value indicating a type of fuel

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: full trailer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A trailer, other than a pole trailer, designed for carrying property and so constructed that no part of its weight rests upon or is carried by the towing road vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: gearbox type value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A value indicating a gearbox type.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: heavy hauler trailer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: trailer whose brakes lines are designed to adapt to separation or extension of the vehicle frame and/or which body consists only of a platform whose primary cargo-carrying surface is not more than 1,016 mm (40 inches) above the ground in an unloaded condition, except that it may include sides that are designed to be easily removable and a permanent “front-end structure”, but that is not a container chassis trailer

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: heavy truck
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A truck which has a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of more than 26,000 pounds (11,793 kilograms).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: road construction controlled horizontal discharge trailer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: trailer or semitrailer that is equipped with a mechanical drive and a conveyor to deliver asphalt and other road building materials, in a controlled horizontal manner, into a lay down machine or paving equipment for road construction and paving operations

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: human powered land vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: land vehicle propelled over ground by human power

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: intercity bus
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A bus used for long-distance passenger transportation between cities over fixed routes with regular schedules.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: kayak
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a small human-powered watercraft that traditionally has a covered deck, and one or more cockpits, each seating one paddler who strokes a double-bladed paddle. In this ontology, kayaks are considered watercrafts of their own kind, not a subtype of boat

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: large bus
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A bus with seating for sixteen or more persons, including the driver.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: large motorcycle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any motorcycle other than a motor-driven cycle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: duży pojazd specjalny
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: special vehicle which is considered large

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: light truck
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A truck which has a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of 10,000 pounds (4,536 kilograms) or less

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: low speed vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A motor vehicle with four or more wheels whose top speed is greater than 20 miles per hour, but not greater than 25 miles per hour.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: medium truck
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A truck which has a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of more than 10,000 pounds and less than or equal to 26,000 pounds (4,536 to 11,793 kilograms).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: modification or maintenance
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: an event in which a part of the vehicle is being replaced or removed, or a new part is being added.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: moped
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A speed-limited motor-driven cycle which may be propelled by pedaling.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: motor-driven cycle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any motorcycle having an engine with less than 150 cubic centimeters displacement or with 5-brake horsepower or less.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: motor boat
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a boat which is powered by an engine

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: motor vehicle in-transport
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: motor vehicle on a roadway or in motion within or outside the trafficway

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: motocykl
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any motor vehicle having a seat or saddle for the use of its operator and designed to travel on not more than three wheels in contact with the ground.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: motorized bicycle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a bicycle with an attached motor used to power the vehicle, or to assist with pedaling

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: motorized road vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any motorized (mechanically or electrically powered) road vehicle not operated on rails.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: my car
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: vehicle that legally belongs to the subject

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: offering
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: thing offered especially as a gift or contribution

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: other bus
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any bus used for transportation purposes other than school bus, transit bus, intercity bus or charter bus.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: ownership info
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a structured value representing information about the period of ownership of a vehicle by a person or organisation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: paint choice or component
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The class of paint choices or components (a "MonoSelectGroup" in automotive terminology), VW ID: 3

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: parked motor vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A motor vehicle not in- transport, other than a working motor vehicle, that is not in motion and not located on the roadway.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: parking choice or component
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The class of parking-related choices or components (a "MonoSelectGroup" in automotive terminology), VW ID: 7

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: parking type
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a type of parking for a vehicle, e.g. in a garage, on the street (open-sky), or in a carport

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: passenger car
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a road motor vehicle, other than a motor cycle, intended for the carriage of passengers and designed to seat no more than nine persons including the driver

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: passenger van
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any van where the area behind the driver or cab is designated for carrying passengers.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: payment method
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: value indicating the payment method of a payment

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: pedalcycle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A non-motorized other road vehicle propelled by pedaling.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: pole trailer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A trailer designed to be attached to the towing road vehicle by means of a reach or pole, or by being boomed or otherwise secured to the towing road vehicle, and ordinarily used for carrying property of a long or irregular shape such as poles, pipes or structural members that are generally capable of sustaining themselves as beams between the supporting connections.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: price specification
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: indication of the unit price and delivery or payment charges

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: property speciﬁcation
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A Property Specification is an abstract entity specifying a set of properties for a vehicle that results from a single choice or the combination of two or more choices and that override the individual properties of the resulting vehicle. Example 1: Power steering and Air conditioning in combination reduce the available engine power from 90 kW to 89 kW. Example 2: Choosing the color option "blue" changes the color of the car to "blue".

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: pulpwood trailer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: trailer or semitrailer that is designed exclusively for harvesting logs or pulpwood and constructed with a skeletal frame with no means for attachment of a solid bed, body, or container

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: quadracycle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a four-wheeled human-powered vehicle. It is also referred to as a quadricycle, quadcycle pedal car or four-wheeled bicycle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: train
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any motorized railway vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: railway vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any land vehicle that is (1) designed primarily for, or in use for, moving persons or property from one place to another on rails and (2) not in use on a land way other than a railway.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: regular vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: normal vehicle used for daily commuting

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: relative price specification
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: relative indication of the unit price and delivery or payment charges

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: rickshaw
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a two-wheeled cart which seats one or two persons and is being drawn by a runner

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: road vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: land vehicle other than a railway vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: roofs choice or component
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The class of roof choices or components (a "MonoSelectGroup" in automotive terminology), VW ID: 5

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: sailing boat
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a boat propelled partly or entirely by sails

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: school bus
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A motor vehicle used for the transportation of any school pupil at or below the 12th-grade level to or from a public or private school or school-related activity.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: seats choice or component
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The class of seat-related choices or components (a "MonoSelectGroup" in automotive terminology), VW ID: 9

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: semitrailer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A trailer, other than a pole trailer, designed for carrying property and so constructed that part of its weight rests upon or is carried by the towing road vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: ship
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a large watercraft that floats on water

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: single unit truck
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A truck consisting primarily of a single motorized transport device designed for carrying property.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: small bus
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A bus with seating for nine to fifteen persons, including the driver.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: mały pojazd specjalny
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: special vehicle which is considered small

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: spec item collection
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A Spec Item Collection is an entity collating multiple coo:ChoiceOrComponent options for a given coo:Derivative, i.e. the available configurational choices. The default choice can be indicated using a coo:default link. All other choices are attached using coo:availableChoice. The number of coo:ChoiceOrComponent items that can / must be selected for a valid configuration are indicated via coo:min and coo:max.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: pojazd specjalny
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a vehicle or trailer intended to perform a special function requiring body adjustments or special equipment; this vehicle is capable of carrying persons and objects associated with the performance of this function

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: species
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: typically a pet, for indicating the type of animals that were regularly transported in the vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed-limited motor-driven cycle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any motor- driven cycle which : 1.) will not attain a speed of more than 30 miles per hour (48 kilometers per hour) in one mile (1.609 kilometers) from a standing start, 2.) has an engine with not more than 50 cubic centimeters displacement or with 2-brake horsepower or less, and 3.) has a power drive system which does not require its operator to shift gears.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: speed interval
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a value indicating a speed interval, mostly for explaining acceleration data

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: steering position value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a value indicating a steering position

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: steering wheels choice or component
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The class of steering wheels choices or components (a "MonoSelectGroup" in automotive terminology), VW ID: 6

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: straddle trailer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: trailer that is designed to transport bulk agricultural commodities from the harvesting location, as evidenced by a framework that is driven over the cargo and lifting arms that suspend the cargo for transit

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: three-wheeled motorcycle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any motor vehicle having a seat or saddle for the use of its operator, and having three wheels in contact with the ground.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: tractor pole trailer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: combination vehicle that carries logs lengthwise so that they form the body of the vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: traffic pattern value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A value indicating a traffic pattern, to be used as a reference for vso:fuelConsumption or vso:fuelEconomy

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: trailer
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A road vehicle designed to be drawn by another road vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: transit bus
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A bus used for passenger transportation over fixed, scheduled routes within primarily urban geographical areas.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: transmission type value
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a value indicating a type of transmission

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: transmission type value automatic
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The class of all automatic transmission types

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: transmission type value manual
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The class of all manual transmission types

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: transport vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Consists of one or more devices or animals and their load.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: trim
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A Trim is an abstract entity specifying (1) the basic features plus (2) a set of configuration choices (mostly non-functional) of a group of vehicles. A Trim should be linked to its Base Model via gr:isVariantOf, if available. Examples: VW Golf S, VW Polo Match, VW Passat SE

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: samochód ciężarowy
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A motor vehicle designed primarily for carrying property.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: truck combination
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A truck consisting primarily of a transport device which is a single- unit truck or truck tractor together with one or more attached trailers.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: truck tractor
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A motor vehicle consisting of a single motorized transport device designed primarily for drawing trailers.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: upholstery choice or component
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The class of upholstery choices or components (a "MonoSelectGroup" in automotive terminology), VW ID: 4

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: utility vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A motor vehicle other than a motorcycle or large bus consisting primarily of a transport device designed for carrying persons, and generally considered a multi-purpose vehicle that is designed to have off-road capabilities.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: van
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of 10,000 pounds or less and is basically a “ box on wheels ” that is identifiable by its enclosed passenger and/or cargo area, step-up floor, and relatively short (or nonexistent) hood.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: van-based bus
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any passenger van designed for carrying nine or more persons, including the driver.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: van-based motorhome
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Any van where a frame-mounted recreational unit is added behind the driver or cab area.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: pojazd
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: a device that is designed or used to transport people or cargo over land, water, air, or through space

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: warranty scope
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: period of time during which the warranty is valid

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: watercraft
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A transport vehicle designed primarily for, or in use for, moving persons or property on or through, and supported by, water from one place to another.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: wheels choice or component
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The class of wheels-related choices or components (a "MonoSelectGroup" in automotive terminology), VW ID: 2

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: working motor vehicle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A motor vehicle in the act of performing construction, maintenance or utility work related to the trafficway.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: ABS
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: portion of a service brake system that automatically controls the degree of rotational wheel slip

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: ADAS
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: broad range of features, including those that provide warnings and/or momentary intervention, such as forward collision warning (FCW) systems, lane keeping assistance (LKA) systems, and automatic emergency braking (AEB) systems, as well as some convenience features that involve Level 1 driver support features, such as ACC and certain parking assistance features

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: acceleration
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Signal/Attribute.Vehicle.Acceleration : Spacial acceleration

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: accelerator
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: pedal that controls the amount of gas being fed into the engine and thereby controls the speed of the vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: active driving assistance system
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: simultaneous use of Lane Centering Assistance and Adaptive Cruise Control features

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: active parking assistance system
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: feature that assists with steering and potentially other functions during parking maneuvers

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: adaptive cruise control system
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: cruise control that also assists with acceleration and/or braking to maintain a driver-selected gap to the vehicle in front

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: air brake system
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: system, including an air-over-hydraulic brake subsystem, that uses air as a medium for transmitting pressure or force from the driver control to the service brake but does not include a system that uses compressed air or vacuum only to assist the driver in applying muscular force to hydraulic or mechanical components

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: air over-hydraulic brake system
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: subsystem of the air brake system that uses compressed air to transmit a force from the driver control to a hydraulic brake system to actuate the service brakes

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: airbag
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: inflatable occupant restraint device that is designed to deploy in a side impact crash to help mitigate occupant injury and/or ejection

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: alternate O2 sensor
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Signal/Attribute.OBD.O2Alt.BankX.SensorX : Alternate oxygen sensor

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: anchor point
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: part of the structure, fitting or attachment on a vehicle or article of cargo to which a tiedown is attached

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: gyro
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Signal/Attribute.Vehicle.AngularVelocity : Spacial rotation

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: automatic disconnect
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: device, that when triggered, conductively separates a high voltage source from the electric power train or the rest of the electric power train

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: automatic emergency braking system
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: feature that detects potential collisions with a vehicle ahead, provides forward collision warning, and automatically brakes to avoid a collision or lessen the severity of impact

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: automatic emergency steering system
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: feature that detects potential collisions with a vehicle ahead and automatically steers to avoid or lessen the severity of impact

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: automatic high beams system
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: feature that switches between high and low beam headlamps automatically based on lighting and traffic

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: autonomous driving chip
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: special system-on-a-chip designed specifically to interpret and recognize, in real-time, traffic-control devices in order to either assist a driver with control of the vehicle or in order to partially or fully automate all aspects of the dynamic driving task

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: auxiliary driving lamp
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: lighting device mounted to provide illumination forward of the vehicle, which supplements the upper beam of a standard headlighting system

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: axle
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: pin or shaft on or with which a wheel or pair of wheels revolves

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: back door
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: door or door system on the back end of a motor vehicle through which passengers can enter or depart the vehicle or cargo can be loaded or unloaded

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: backup camera system
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: feature that displays the area behind the vehicle when in reverse gear

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: backup lamp
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: lamp that illuminates the road to the rear of a vehicle and provides a warning signal to pedestrians and other drivers when the vehicle is backing up or is about to back up

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: battery management
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: device or solution that manages battery performance, including controlling the charging and discharging of batteries, electrochemical cells, and fuel cells

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: bead
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: part of the tire made of steel wires, wrapped or reinforced by ply cords, that is shaped to fit the rim

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: bias ply tire
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: pneumatic tire in which the ply cords that extend to the beads are laid at alternate angles substantially less than 90° to the centerline of the tread

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: blind spot warning system
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: feature that detects vehicles in the blind spot while driving and notifies the driver to their presence

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: blocking
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: structure, device, or another substantial article placed against or around an article of cargo to prevent horizontal movement of the article of cargo

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: body
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: outer panels that shroud a vehicle's mechanical and electrical workings

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: booster seat

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: acceleration time
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition:
The time needed to accelerate the vehicle from a given start velocity to a given target velocity.

Typical unit code(s): SEC for seconds

  • Note: There are unfortunately no standard unit codes for seconds/0..100 km/h or seconds/0..60 mph. Simply use "SEC" for seconds and indicate the velocities in the name of the QuantitativeValue, or use valueReference with a QuantitativeValue of 0..60 mph or 0..100 km/h to specify the reference speeds.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: advanced payment
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Indicates the advanced payment for the financing

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: available choice
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: This property links available Choices or Components to a Spec Item.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: body style
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Indicates the design and body style of the vehicle (e.g. station wagon, hatchback, etc.).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: cargo volume
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The available volume for cargo or luggage. For automobiles, this is usually the trunk volume. Typical unit code(s): LTR for liters, FTQ for cubic foot/feet Note: You can use minValue and maxValue to indicate ranges.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: carried out by
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The business or type of business that carried out the check, repair, maintenance, or modification

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: compatibility
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Links from a Derivative to information on whether a particular configuration is valid (true) or invalid (false)

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: compatible with
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Indicates that two Choices or Components are compatible with each other. Note: This property is symmetric, i.e., if A is compatible with B, then B is also compatible with A.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: contains
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: A naive part-whole relation that allows providing more granular uco:OwnershipInfo data for a part of the duration of the ownership

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: credit
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Indicates the credit for the financing

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: current location
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The current location of the vehicle, i.e. where the car could be tested. For indicating alternative locations to which the seller is willing to bring the car, use gr:availableAtOrFrom attached to the gr:Offering, since those are aspects of the offer, not of the vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: current owner
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: This property points to the current owner of the vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: customer cash price
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Indicates the customer cash price for the financing

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: customer deposit
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Indicates the customer deposit for the financing

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: default
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: This property links the default Choice or Component to a Spec Item. Since it is defined a sub-property of coo:availableChoice, the default choice is automatically part of the available choices.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: depends on
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Links a Choice or Component to one or multiple other Choices Or Components required for that choice Note: This property is transitive, i.e., if B is required by A and C and D are required by B, then C and D are also required by A.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: deposit contribution
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Indicates the deposit contribution for the financing

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: discount
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Indicates the discount for the financing

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: drive wheel configuration
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The drive wheel configuration, i.e. which roadwheels will receive torque from the vehicle's engine via the drivetrain

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: driver
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: This property points to the driver or drivers that were regularly driving the vehicle during the respective period of time (when attached to uco:OwnershipInfo) or in total (when attached directly to a vso:Vehicle).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: engine displacement
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition:
The volume swept by all of the pistons inside the cylinders of an internal combustion engine in a single movement.

Typical unit code(s): CMQ for cubic centimeter, LTR for liters, INQ for cubic inches * Note 1: You can link to information about how the given value has been determined using the valueReference property. * Note 2: You can use minValue and maxValue to indicate ranges.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: engine power
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition:
The power of the vehicle's engine. Typical unit code(s): KWT for kilowatt, BHP for brake horsepower, N12 for metric horsepower (PS, with 1 PS = 735,49875 W)

  • Note 1: There are many different ways of measuring an engine's power. For an overview, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsepower#Enginepowertest_codes.
  • Note 2: You can link to information about how the given value has been determined using the valueReference property.
  • Note 3: You can use minValue and maxValue to indicate ranges.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: engine type
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The type of engine or engines powering the vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: event information
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: This property points to events related to the vehicle, like accidents and damages or major modifications or maintenance.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: excess mileage
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Indicates the rate for excess mileage

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: feature
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Indicates a built-in feature, accessory, or component of the vehicle. Use DBPedia resources to indicate the features, if possible. Popular identifiers are http://dbpedia.org/resource/Anti-lock_braking_system http://dbpedia.org/resource/Electronic_stability_control http://dbpedia.org/resource/Armrest http://dbpedia.org/resource/Spoiler_%28automotive%29 http://dbpedia.org/resource/CD_Changer http://dbpedia.org/resource/Cup_holder http://dbpedia.org/resource/Tow_hitch http://dbpedia.org/resource/Power_window http://dbpedia.org/resource/Power_steering http://dbpedia.org/resource/Air_conditioner http://dbpedia.org/resource/Child_safety_lock http://dbpedia.org/resource/Parking_sensors See also http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Automotive_accessories. If you cannot find a suitable identifier in DBPedia, define your own as an instance of vso:FeatureValue.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: feature override
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Links a coo:ConfigurationInfo node to information on how a choice or component or the combination of multiple choices will override the regular properties of the resulting vehicle

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: final payment fee
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Indicates the final payment fee for the financing

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: first monthly payment fee
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Indicates the first monthly payment fee for the financing

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: fuel capacity
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition:
The capacity of the fuel tank or in the case of electric cars, the battery. If there are multiple components for storage, this should indicate the total of all storage of the same type.

Typical unit code(s): LTR for liters, GLL of US gallons, GLI for UK / imperial gallons, AMH for ampere-hours (for electrical vehicles).

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: fuel consumption
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The amount of fuel consumed for traveling a particular distance or temporal duration with the given vehicle (e.g. liters per 100 km). Note 1: There are unfortunately no standard unit codes for liters per 100 km. Use unitText to indicate the unit of measurement, e.g. L/100 km. Note 2: There are two ways of indicating the fuel consumption, fuelConsumption (e.g. 8 liters per 100 km) and fuelEfficiency (e.g. 30 miles per gallon). They are reciprocal. Note 3: Often, the absolute value is useful only when related to driving speed ("at 80 km/h") or usage pattern ("city traffic"). You can use valueReference to link the value for the fuel consumption to another value.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: fuel type
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The type of fuel suitable for the engine or engines of the vehicle. Use DBPedia resources to indicate the fuel type. Popular identifiers are http://dbpedia.org/resource/Gasoline http://dbpedia.org/resource/Diesel http://dbpedia.org/resource/Biodiesel http://dbpedia.org/resource/Kerosene For two-stroke mixtures, use vso:TwoStrokeMixture.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: gearbox
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: The gearbox type of the vehicle or vehicle model

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: has complete car model
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Links one or multiple Complete Car Models to the underlying Derivative

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Links a Derivative to a Trim

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: has ownership info
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: This property points to information about the current and previous owners of the vehicle.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: has spec item choice
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: Links a Complete Car Model to the choices for configurational options

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: has spec items
https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.definition: This property links available Spec Items to a Derivative.

https://spec.edmcouncil.org/auto/ontolog.label: has trim
